title: Plagues of Livestock, Boils, and Hail

questions.question: What did the fifth plague strike in Egypt?
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:6 (ESV): "All the livestock of the Egyptians died, but not one of the livestock of the Israelites died."

questions.question: What did the sixth plague bring upon people and animals?
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:10 (ESV): "It became boils breaking out in sores on man and beast."

questions.question: What was the seventh plague?
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:23 (ESV): "The Lord sent thunder and hail, and fire ran down to the earth."

questions.question: Were the Israelites affected by the plague on livestock?
options: Yes, all their animals died too
No, not one of their livestock died
Only some of their animals died
questions.correctAnswer: No, not one of their livestock died
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:6-7 (ESV): "Not one of the livestock of the people of Israel was dead."

questions.question: What did some of Pharaoh's servants do to escape the hail?
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:20 (ESV): "Then whoever feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh hurried his slaves and his livestock into the houses."

questions.question: What came with the hail that struck Egypt?
options: Fire running down to the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Fire running down to the earth
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:24 (ESV): "There was hail and fire flashing continually in the midst of the hail."

questions.question: What did Pharaoh admit after the hail?
options: That the Lord is righteous and he and his people are wicked
questions.correctAnswer: That the Lord is righteous and he and his people are wicked
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:27 (ESV): "Pharaoh said, 'This time I have sinned; the Lord is in the right, and I and my people are in the wrong.'"

questions.question: Why did Moses throw soot from the kiln for the boils?
options: As a demonstration of God's power
questions.correctAnswer: As a demonstration of God's power
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:8-9 (ESV): "Take handfuls of soot from the kiln... and it shall become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and become boils."

questions.question: Could the magicians stand before Moses during the plague of boils?
options: No, because of the boils that were on them
questions.correctAnswer: No, because of the boils that were on them
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:11 (ESV): "The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils."

questions.question: Which crops were destroyed by the hail?
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:31-32 (ESV): "The flax and the barley were struck down... But the wheat and the emmer were not struck down."

questions.question: What famous verse about God's purpose appears in Exodus 9?
options: "I have raised you up to show my power"
questions.correctAnswer: "I have raised you up to show my power"
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:16 (ESV): "But for this purpose I have raised you up, to show you my power, so that my name may be proclaimed in all the earth."

questions.question: What did Moses say about Pharaoh when the hail stopped?
options: Pharaoh and his servants still did not fear the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh and his servants still did not fear the Lord
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:30 (ESV): "But as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear the Lord God."

questions.question: Why were wheat and emmer (spelt) not destroyed by the hail?
options: They had not yet grown up (late crops)
questions.correctAnswer: They had not yet grown up (late crops)
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:32 (ESV): "But the wheat and the emmer were not struck down, for they are late in coming up."

questions.question: According to Exodus 9:14, why was God sending all these plagues?
options: So Pharaoh would know there is none like God in all the earth
To take revenge on the Egyptians
questions.correctAnswer: So Pharaoh would know there is none like God in all the earth
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:14 (ESV): "That you may know that there is none like me in all the earth."

questions.question: What did God say He could have done to wipe out Egypt but chose not to?
options: Stretched out His hand to strike with pestilence and cut them off
Opened the earth to swallow them
questions.correctAnswer: Stretched out His hand to strike with pestilence and cut them off
questions.explanation: Exodus 9:15 (ESV): "For by now I could have put out my hand and struck you and your people with pestilence, and you would have been cut off from the earth."

key_verse_text: But for this purpose I have raised you up, to show you my power, so that my name may be proclaimed in all the earth.
